title: U.S. House · New York's 9th Congressional District
area: Central Brooklyn, including Flatbush, East Flatbush, Crown Heights, Midwood, and Park Slope.

context.text: Incumbent Yvette D. Clarke defeated Michael Goldfarb and Joshua Bristol in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 68.4% to 15.4% to 14.9%. Joel Anabilah-Azumah advanced unopposed from the canceled Republican and Conservative Party primaries; fellow Republican filer Lewis Mizrahi (also the R/C nominee in NY-8) was disqualified from this district's Republican primary.

candidates.name: Yvette D. Clarke
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 68.4% of the vote

summary.text: Yvette D. Clarke is the incumbent U.S. Representative for NY-9, first elected to Congress in 2012 after representing the former NY-11 district (2007-2013) and serving on the New York City Council (2000-2007). She sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

background.text: Born in Brooklyn; attended Oberlin College from 1982 to 1986.
Served as director of business development for the Bronx Economic Development Corporation (Bronx Empowerment Zone) before entering elected office.
Served on the New York City Council from 2000 to 2007, representing a Brooklyn district that included Flatbush and Crown Heights.
Represented New York's 11th Congressional District from 2007 to 2013 before redistricting; has represented the 9th District since 2013.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 (119th Congress) session, serves on the Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade subcommittee, its Communications and Technology subcommittee, and its Oversight and Investigations subcommittee.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 9733, the Interagency Council on Affordable Housing Act of 2026, introduced July 16, 2026.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 9014, the Affordable Housing and Area Median Income Fairness Act of 2026.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 9090, the Advancing Menopause Care and Mid-Life Women's Health Act.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 10489, the American Renewable Energy Act of 2026.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 8811, the Moms Matter Act, and H.R. 9457, the Diversity Visa Protection and Modernization Act, in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Joel Anabilah-Azumah

summary.text: Joel Anabilah-Azumah is a small-business owner in transportation who has run against Yvette Clarke in NY-9 in five consecutive elections (2018, 2020, 2022 for U.S. Senate, 2024, and 2026), running as a Republican in 2026. He describes himself as focused on personal freedom, opposing foreign military intervention, and resisting the use of artificial intelligence in government functions.

background.text: Born in New York, NY; earned a bachelor's degree from Union College in 2005; career in the transportation industry.

Previously ran for the same NY-9 seat in 2018 (Reform Party, lost to Clarke 89.3%-10.3%-0.4%), 2020 (Serve America Movement Party, lost to Clarke), and in 2022 ran for U.S. Senate (withdrew); withdrew from the 2024 NY-9 race as well before running again in 2026.

priorities.text: "I will fight all attempts to outsource government functions to artificial intelligence. Humans must be in charge of governing other humans at all times."
"I will resist all attempts to drag the United States into unnecessary and unwinnable military conflicts."
"I will ensure that citizens of the United States have the ability to speak freely, even when their statements are unpopular."

positions.summary: Says he will resist U.S. involvement in unnecessary and unwinnable foreign military conflicts generally, though he did not name Israel specifically; his stated foreign-policy focus is on avoiding new wars rather than a position on any single conflict.
positions.quote: I will resist all attempts to drag the United States into unnecessary and unwinnable military conflicts.

candidates.researchNotes: Anabilah-Azumah has not held elected office, so there is no official governing record to cite. His views above come from Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, which he completed in May 2026; FEC filings show $0 in recorded contributions for his 2026 campaign as of the most recent disclosure period covered by Ballotpedia.
